title: The deer
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Friday. Then deer. The first one: a photograph of a buck on a tailgate, a man beside it in a mill jacket, brought in by the man. Wood frames it in cedar without a word and the man says nothing and it's the same as May and it's not. The cover is the tailgate, no deer.

panels.composition: The shop. A MAN in a faded mill jacket with a photograph: a buck on a tailgate, himself beside it. The OWNER at her station. WOOD at the counter.

image.prompt: a man in a faded mill jacket handing a photograph across a frame shop counter to a young man, a woman in reading glasses at her station, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The photo: the buck, the tailgate, the man's hand on the antler. Pride drawn as a hand.

image.prompt: close on a photograph of a deer on a pickup tailgate with a man's hand resting on its antler, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood choosing cedar. No mat. Not a word. The man nodding once.

image.prompt: a young man selecting a plain cedar frame without speaking while a man in a mill jacket nods, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The cover, that night: the tailgate, empty, the truck's bed, rain. No deer. The strip drew the pride and left the deer out.

image.prompt: close on a photocopied booklet cover showing an empty pickup tailgate in rain, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen over rough blue pencil; xerox grain; stark spotting; rain in frantic vertical hatching (Arc 1's aesthetic)

notes: Then deer. Cedar, no mat, no word; the same as May and not. The tailgate without the deer.
